title: Supply chain and CI/CD
status: AUTHORED. Your target's dependency graph is part of your target.

atom_notes.A11: an upstream artefact is trusted and is not trustworthy, which is the whole domain
atom_notes.A08: SBOMs and lockfiles are exposure, and are often public by default
atom_notes.A15: pipeline configuration is where the trust decision actually lives
atom_notes.A09: signing and provenance make the trust decision checkable

required_cells.why: inventory the dependency graph and the pipeline before testing either
scanning at scale needs automation with a real oracle, not a CVE count
dependency confusion or a poisoned action is the exploitation step
prove the artefact was pulled, not merely referenced
verify the fix: pinned, signed and reachable from the registry

entries.name: Install time execution surface
entries.role: What runs when a dependency is installed, before anyone reviews its behaviour. An install hook is code execution with the developer's authority.
preconditions: the project installs dependencies from a registry
oracle: a network request or file write observed during install, attributable to a package
the same install with scripts disabled produces none

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Workflow trigger trust
entries.role: Which events can start a job and what that job can reach. A pull request from a fork running with secrets is the whole class.
preconditions: CI runs on contributions from outside the repository
oracle: a secret present in a job triggered by an unprivileged actor, or provably absent
the event, the actor and the permissions recorded per run

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Lockfile enforcement
entries.role: Whether the resolved version can drift from the locked one. A lock that install ignores is documentation, not a control.
preconditions: the project ships a lockfile
oracle: an install resolves exactly the locked versions, verified by diffing the tree
a registry substitution attempt either fails or is recorded

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Subresource integrity and third party pinning
entries.role: Whether a third party script can change under the site. Without a pin, the third party's compromise is your compromise.
preconditions: the page loads script from an origin you do not control
oracle: a modified third party file is refused by the browser
every third party script tag carries an integrity value or an equivalent pin

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Deployment credential lifetime and scope
entries.role: What a deploy can reach and for how long. A long lived shared credential turns one pipeline compromise into permanent access.
preconditions: a pipeline deploys to an environment
oracle: the credential is scoped to the artefact it ships, demonstrated by a refused action outside it
its lifetime is stated and enforced, with a rotation event recorded

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Repository exposure history
entries.role: Whether a repository was ever public, and whether forks and history still hold what was removed.
preconditions: the project has had secrets or internal detail in its history
oracle: a secret found in history after removal from the working tree
a fork or mirror still serving content the origin no longer has

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Maintainer account and release authority
entries.role: Who can publish a new version of a dependency, and whether that requires a second party. A single unprotected account with publish rights is the whole attack surface for a popular package.
preconditions: a dependency's repository and registry settings are visible
oracle: the number of accounts with publish rights, and whether any lacks a second factor
a release published without a second approver, shown from the release record
branch protection on the release path, read rather than assumed

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Artefact provenance and rebuild agreement
entries.role: Whether the published artefact can be rebuilt from the stated source. Without that, a registry compromise and a source compromise look identical from the outside.
preconditions: the project publishes binaries, images or packages
oracle: a rebuild from the stated commit producing byte identical or functionally identical output
a provenance attestation naming the builder and the source digest
a published artefact that does not match its own provenance, which is the finding

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Signed history and protected refs
entries.role: Whether commits and tags are signed and whether the platform enforces it. An unsigned history means a rewritten branch is indistinguishable from the original.
preconditions: the repository has a release process
oracle: a signature verified on the tag that shipped, not only on commits
a direct push or force push refused by policy, demonstrated
an unsigned commit rejected at merge

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Vendored code and binary trust
entries.role: Whether code committed inside the tree is reviewed as code or ignored as third party. Vendored dependencies and binaries are where review stops.
preconditions: the repository vendors dependencies or ships binaries
oracle: a change to vendored code that was reviewed, shown by the pull request trail
a binary in the tree traceable to a source and a build, or listed as untraceable
a submodule pinned to a commit rather than to a branch

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Generated code, model and tool definition provenance
entries.role: Anything that arrives already written and is trusted because a tool or a model produced it. Generated code, model files and remote tool definitions all carry authoring authority without the review that code normally gets.
preconditions: the project contains generated code, model artefacts or remote tool definitions
oracle: a generated file with no recorded generator and version
a model artefact whose publisher cannot be verified
a tool definition fetched at runtime rather than pinned in the repository

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Plugin and extension review path
entries.role: Whether a plugin is reviewed before publication and again on update. A marketplace that reviews once and never again is a delivery channel for whoever takes over the plugin later.
preconditions: the product loads plugins or extensions from a marketplace
oracle: an update that changed behaviour without a review record
a publisher whose ownership changed without a re-review
the review criteria written down, so a reviewer can apply them

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Dependency incident response
entries.role: Whether the organisation can answer what uses a given package, at which version, in what timeframe. That question arrives on the day of an advisory and cannot be answered retroactively.
preconditions: the project has a dependency inventory
oracle: the exposure list produced for a named package inside a stated window, measured
every system on the list confirmed from its own lockfile rather than from a spreadsheet
the same query run before an incident, as a rehearsal

tree.q: What is the trust decision: a package, an action, or a build?
tree.why: Three different supply chains with three different checks. Most reviews only cover packages and call it done.

branches.action: check registry priority and namespace scope, then whether a private name could resolve publicly
branches.oracle: a package resolved from the wrong registry

branches.action: an action is code executed with your token. read what it does and check whether the tag is mutable
branches.oracle: mutable tag or unreviewed action executing

branches.action: provenance and signing. an unsigned artefact is a claim, not a fact
branches.oracle: signature verified against the expected identity

branches.action: scan the repo and the bundle, then verify the secret is live

mirror.detect: a private name resolved from the public registry
a name one character from a popular package

mirror.control: strip version detail from public artefacts

gaps.gap: No tool that answers 'could this private name resolve publicly' before the attack
gaps.build_candidate: check each scoped dependency name against the public registry and report collisions

gaps.gap: No single check that a fix is pinned AND signed AND reachable
gaps.build_candidate: three check pipeline per dependency: pinned, signature valid, source reachable
the three check pipeline above, run as a retest
